newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan low rates won't persist if economy firms-EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan low rates won't persist if economy firms-EPA.

text.p: Japan's extremely low interest rate levels will not persist if a self-sustainable economic recovery centred on domestic demand can be confirmed, Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Vice Minister Shimpei Nukaya told a news conference on Tuesday morning.

"I don't think low interest rates will persist endlessly if we can confirm a self-sustainable recovery centred on private-sector demand. It is up to the BOJ (Bank of Japan) to decide (interest rates levels or the timing of rate changes)," Nukaya said.

He also said that EPA Minister Taro Aso's comments in an interview with a news wire in New York on Monday probably meant the same thing -- that if Japan's economic recovery became firmer, low rate levels would not continue for long.

BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita, who attended the morning's meeting of economic ministers, was quoted by Nukaya as saying that long-term interest rates and stock prices are rather weak due to data which has shown that the increase in Japan's consumption tax is still having a lingering effect on consumption.
Nukaya said the basic trend in the Japanese economy is holding firm, with private-sector capital spending firming up.
Housing construction may continue to be weak and needs to be monitored carefully, he added.
He said the EPA holds the view that Japan's economy is going to pick up in the latter half of the current fiscal year, which began on April 1.
Nukaya added that a minority of private economists believe the Japanese economy may contract.
Improvements in the incomes of wage earners and in employment are likely to support Japan's overall private consumption, he said.
